questions.prompt: Find the arc length of \(y=3x+1\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=2\).
questions.answer: We use the arc length formula \(L=\int_a^b\sqrt{1+(dy/dx)^2}\,dx\). For \(y=3x+1\), \(dy/dx=3\). Thus \(L=\int_0^2\sqrt{1+3^2}\,dx=\int_0^2\sqrt{10}\,dx\). This equals \(2\sqrt{10}\). Therefore the arc length is \(2\sqrt{10}\) units.

questions.prompt: Find the arc length of \(y=\frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=3\).
questions.answer: We use \(L=\int_a^b\sqrt{1+(dy/dx)^2}\,dx\). Since \(y=\frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\), \(dy/dx=\sqrt{x}\). Therefore \(L=\int_0^3\sqrt{1+x}\,dx\). Integrating gives \([\frac{2}{3}(1+x)^{3/2}]_0^3=\frac{2}{3}(8-1)=14/3\). Therefore the arc length is \(\frac{14}{3}\) units.

questions.prompt: Find the arc length of \(x=y^2/2\) from \(y=0\) to \(y=2\).
questions.answer: Because \(x\) is given as a function of \(y\), use \(L=\int_c^d\sqrt{1+(dx/dy)^2}\,dy\). Here \(dx/dy=y\), so \(L=\int_0^2\sqrt{1+y^2}\,dy\). An antiderivative is \(\frac{1}{2}(y\sqrt{1+y^2}+\ln(y+\sqrt{1+y^2}))\). Evaluating from \(0\) to \(2\) gives \(\sqrt{5}+\frac{1}{2}\ln(2+\sqrt{5})\). Therefore the arc length is \(\sqrt{5}+\frac{1}{2}\ln(2+\sqrt{5})\) units.

questions.prompt: Find the arc length of \(y=\ln(\cos x)\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=\pi/4\).
questions.answer: We use \(L=\int_a^b\sqrt{1+(dy/dx)^2}\,dx\). For \(y=\ln(\cos x)\), \(dy/dx=-\tan x\). Then \(\sqrt{1+\tan^2 x}=\sec x\) on the given interval. Thus \(L=\int_0^{\pi/4}\sec x\,dx\). Since \(\int\sec x\,dx=\ln|\sec x+\tan x|\), the length is \([\ln(\sec x+\tan x)]_0^{\pi/4}=\ln(\sqrt{2}+1)\). Therefore the arc length is \(\ln(1+\sqrt{2})\) units.

questions.prompt: Find the arc length of \(y=\cosh x\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=1\).
questions.answer: We use the arc length formula. Since \(d(\cosh x)/dx=\sinh x\), the integrand is \(\sqrt{1+\sinh^2 x}\). The identity \(\cosh^2 x-\sinh^2 x=1\) gives \(\sqrt{1+\sinh^2 x}=\cosh x\). Hence \(L=\int_0^1\cosh x\,dx=[\sinh x]_0^1=\sinh 1\). Therefore the arc length is \(\sinh 1\) units.

questions.prompt: Find the arc length of the upper semicircle \(y=\sqrt{9-x^2}\) from \(x=-3\) to \(x=3\).
questions.answer: The graph is the upper half of the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\), so the radius is \(3\). The full circumference of a circle is \(2\pi r\), and the upper semicircle has half that length. Therefore \(L=\frac{1}{2}(2\pi\cdot 3)=3\pi\). The arc length is \(3\pi\) units.

questions.prompt: Find the exact arc length of \(y=x^2\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=1\).
questions.answer: We use \(L=\int_0^1\sqrt{1+(dy/dx)^2}\,dx\). Since \(dy/dx=2x\), \(L=\int_0^1\sqrt{1+4x^2}\,dx\). An antiderivative is \(\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{1+4x^2}+\frac{1}{4}\ln(2x+\sqrt{1+4x^2})\). Evaluating from \(0\) to \(1\) gives \(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\ln(2+\sqrt{5})\). Therefore the exact arc length is \(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\ln(2+\sqrt{5})\) units.

questions.prompt: A parametric curve is defined by \(x=t^2\) and \(y=t^3\) for \(0 \le t \le 1\). Find its arc length.
questions.answer: For a parametric curve, \(L=\int_a^b\sqrt{(dx/dt)^2+(dy/dt)^2}\,dt\). Here \(dx/dt=2t\) and \(dy/dt=3t^2\). Thus \(L=\int_0^1\sqrt{4t^2+9t^4}\,dt=\int_0^1 t\sqrt{4+9t^2}\,dt\), since \(t\ge 0\). Let \(u=4+9t^2\), so \(du=18t\,dt\). Then \(L=\frac{1}{18}\int_4^{13}u^{1/2}\,du=\frac{1}{27}(13^{3/2}-8)\). Therefore the arc length is \(\frac{13\sqrt{13}-8}{27}\) units.

questions.prompt: Set up, but do not evaluate, the integral for the arc length of \(y=e^{-x^2}\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=2\).
questions.answer: We are asked only to set up the arc length integral. The formula is \(L=\int_a^b\sqrt{1+(dy/dx)^2}\,dx\). For \(y=e^{-x^2}\), the chain rule gives \(dy/dx=-2xe^{-x^2}\). Therefore \((dy/dx)^2=4x^2e^{-2x^2}\). The required setup is \(L=\int_0^2\sqrt{1+4x^2e^{-2x^2}}\,dx\). This is the complete arc length integral for the stated curve and interval.

questions.prompt: A learner finds the arc length of \(y=2x\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=5\) by computing \(\int_0^5(1+2^2)\,dx=25\). Explain the error and find the correct arc length.
questions.answer: The error is omitting the square root in the arc length formula. The correct formula is \(L=\int_a^b\sqrt{1+(dy/dx)^2}\,dx\). For \(y=2x\), \(dy/dx=2\), so \(L=\int_0^5\sqrt{1+2^2}\,dx=\int_0^5\sqrt{5}\,dx\). Therefore \(L=5\sqrt{5}\). The correct arc length is \(5\sqrt{5}\) units.
